stories.h: Tinubu unveils models of new Nigerian satellites
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday unveiled models of Nigeria's new optical and radar satellites at an event in Abuja, Punch reported. According to the report, the satellites are intended to strengthen national security, improve environmental monitoring and help grow the country's space economy. Further details of the programme were not yet available.

stories.h: Naira falls to eight-month low despite CBN sales
stories.p: The naira weakened 2.5% to N1,394 per dollar at the official market last Friday, its lowest in eight months, according to FMDQ data cited by Legit.ng. Weekly forex turnover rose 36.6% to $4.67bn even though the CBN sold about $1.30bn. Gross reserves dipped to $54.65bn. Analysts blamed investor demand and festive imports.

stories.h: NDC boycotts IGP's security meeting with parties
stories.p: The Nigeria Democratic Congress said it would boycott the Inspector-General of Police's security meeting with political parties on Tuesday. The party accused the police of failing to protect its members from attacks it blamed on ruling APC thugs, saying it would not lend legitimacy to the process. The APC's response was not included in the report.

stories.h: Delta rally violence: police confirm six dead
stories.p: Police have confirmed that six people died in violence at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State, on Monday. IGP Olatunji Disu ordered an impartial investigation, while Governor Sheriff Oborevwori visited the community on Tuesday and promised that those responsible would face justice.

stories.h: CBN keeps benchmark interest rate at 23%
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria kept its Monetary Policy Rate at 23% after its 308th MPC meeting in Abuja, Governor Olayemi Cardoso announced on Tuesday. He pointed to five straight months of falling inflation, now 14.06% in October. Cash reserve ratios stay at 45% for commercial banks and 16% for merchant banks.

stories.h: Defence chief warns media over military operations
stories.p: Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Olufemi Oluyede on Tuesday urged journalists not to reveal troop movements, operational locations or military capabilities, saying such reports can endanger soldiers. Speaking at a Defence Headquarters communication workshop in Abuja, he also warned about old videos and AI-made fake content and urged checks before publishing.

stories.h: Tinubu asks Reps to approve revised federal laws
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to approve the revised Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025 edition. In a letter read by the Speaker on Tuesday, he said the review removes 268 obsolete laws and keeps 664 principal enactments, along with 731 pieces of subsidiary legislation.

stories.h: Tinubu proposes N3.15tn cut to 2026 budget
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to cut the 2026 federal budget by N3.15 trillion, from N68.32 trillion to N65.18 trillion, while keeping the N31.46 trillion deficit. He sent a bill to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, with a revised fiscal framework for the year.

stories.h: Plateau governor says state police will tackle insecurity
stories.p: Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang says a well-structured state police would help address insecurity in the state. He spoke in Jos while receiving the preliminary report of the advisory committee on state policing.

stories.h: Lagos Assembly advances new tenancy bill
stories.p: The Lagos State House of Assembly on Tuesday adopted its Housing Committee's report on the Lagos State Tenancy Bill, 2025. The bill would set out the rights and duties of landlords and tenants and the procedure for recovering premises. Committee chair Olusegun Ege presented the report, with Speaker Mudashiru Obasa presiding.

stories.h: France and Nigeria sign three agribusiness agreements
stories.p: France and Nigeria have signed three agribusiness agreements and set out an energy roadmap at French Week 2026 in Lagos, organised by the FNCCI. The event also hosted a French Tech Summit, where French investors and Nigerian startups discussed areas where they could work together.

stories.h: Court voids Omo-Agege's NDC Delta Central ticket
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Warri on Tuesday nullified former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege's nomination as NDC candidate for Delta Central in 2027. The judge ordered INEC to remove his name, ruling the party had not filed a valid membership register before its primary. The suit was filed by Prof. Alexander Akpodiete.

stories.h: Morocco accuses Senegal FA chief in AFCON row
stories.p: Morocco's football federation has alleged that Senegal FA president Abdoulaye Fall phoned an arbitrator at the Court of Arbitration for Sport handling the disputed 2025 AFCON final. Senegal denies the claim. CAS was expected to give its ruling on Tuesday, though reports said Morocco's objection could delay it.

stories.h: EU launches fund for women facing poll violence
stories.p: Team Europe on Tuesday launched a €100,000 (about N152.9 million) rapid response fund in Abuja for women threatened by election-related violence before the 2027 polls. Running until March 2027, it covers medical, legal, counselling, safe housing and transport help. Organisers said it cannot be used for campaign funding.

stories.h: IGP Disu warns parties against campaign violence
stories.p: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu on Tuesday warned political parties, candidates and supporters against sponsoring violence, hiring thugs or using weapons to intimidate opponents ahead of the 2027 elections. Speaking at a high-level security meeting, he said no one is above the law and promised the police would stay neutral and professional.

stories.h: Ex-CJN Ariwoola warns against post-election violence in 2027
stories.p: Former Chief Justice of Nigeria Olukayode Ariwoola has warned against a repeat of the killings that followed the 2011 elections. He urged action to curb political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: WHO: Ebola responders trapped in DR Congo by fighting
stories.p: The World Health Organization says Ebola responders are trapped in the Democratic Republic of Congo because of heavy fighting. The WHO blamed the country's failure to contain the virus on insecurity.

stories.h: Lagos residents can now report poor artisan services
stories.p: The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) says residents with problems with tailors, plumbers, electricians, mechanics, carpenters, painters or air-conditioner repairers can report them. The agency offers complaint channels and mediation, especially where artisans delay jobs or abandon work after being paid.

stories.h: Indonesia factory fire death toll rises to 26
stories.p: Police in Indonesia say 26 people have now died in a fire at a factory, and another 28 people remain unaccounted for. Officials said an investigation has been opened into what caused the blaze. Rescue and search efforts were continuing at the site, Channels Television reported on Tuesday.

stories.h: US adds 24 Nigerians to deportation list
stories.p: The United States Department of Homeland Security has added 24 more Nigerians to its 'Worst of the Worst' list of foreign nationals facing removal from the country. Several Nigerian outlets reported on Tuesday that the new names bring the total number of Nigerians on the list to 157.

stories.h: Lagos Assembly backs raising magistrates' retirement age to 65
stories.p: The Lagos State House of Assembly has adopted a committee report on amending the Magistrates' Courts Law, 2015, which proposes raising magistrates' retirement age to 65. The report, adopted at Monday's plenary, aims to strengthen the magistracy and improve the administration of justice in the state.

stories.h: INEC to test BVAS in nationwide mock accreditation on Saturday
stories.p: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will hold a nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise with BVAS machines on Saturday, November 28, in selected polling units, including 490 in Lagos State. INEC has published the list of polling units and the hours as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Benue police arrest two suspects linked to Abuja robbery
stories.p: The Benue State Police Command says it has arrested two suspected members of an interstate robbery gang and recovered a stolen Camry car. Police linked the suspects to a robbery in Wuse 2, Abuja. Punch reports that one suspect later died after fleeing and being rearrested.

stories.h: 4,000 flood-hit Ogun farmers get farm support
stories.p: The National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) has given emergency support to 4,000 smallholder farmers in Ogun State whose farms were damaged by this year's rainy-season floods. The 2,800 rice farmers and 1,200 maize farmers are receiving fertilisers, herbicides and pesticides to help them recover.

stories.h: Infantino says Nigeria is not ready to host a World Cup
stories.p: FIFA President Gianni Infantino says Nigeria is not yet equipped to host the FIFA World Cup, pointing to gaps in stadiums, airports and transport networks. He gave the assessment in an interview with ARISE News in Abuja on Monday, when asked whether the country could host the tournament.

stories.h: Court freezes N135.5bn held by Nigerian Governors' Forum
stories.p: An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on about N135.5 billion (around $100m) held by the Nigerian Governors' Forum in a dispute over Paris Club refunds. The order stops the forum's trustees from withdrawing, moving or otherwise dealing with the money.
